description.narrative: TradeMark Africa's Physical Connectivity Portfolio works to close Africa's critical trade infrastructure gap, where road transport costs represent approximately 29% of the price of goods traded within the continent compared to just 7% for goods traded outside Africa, by investing in the ports, borders, roads, and trade corridors that determine how quickly and cheaply goods move across the continent. Since 2010, the Portfolio has constructed or operationalised over 20 One Stop Border Posts across East Africa and the Horn of Africa, reducing average crossing times, while port interventions at Mombasa and Dar es Salaam contributed to dwell times falling and annual cargo volume growing. The Portfolio operates through three complementary financing models, grant-based funding for projects essential to regional integration that are not commercially viable; hybrid viability gap funding to make marginally viable projects bankable; and catalytic commercial capital mobilised through Trade Catalyst Africa (TCA), TMA's dedicated capital facility, reflecting the reality that Africa's annual infrastructure financing gap of $68–108 billion cannot be closed through grants alone. Guided by a 2023–2030 strategy, the Portfolio continues to target the most significant constraints to trade flows across roads, ports, inland waterways, and border posts, with a growing emphasis on intermodal integration, linking maritime, road, rail, and air transport system

recipient-country.narrative: TradeMark Africa (TMA) accelerates economic integration across 20 sub-Saharan nations by designing regional programmes that reduce trade barriers, lower transit costs, and digitize border infrastructure. Spanning East, West, Central, Southern Africa, and the Horn, these initiatives modernise critical maritime ports and key trade corridors by replacing paper-heavy customs processes with automated digital single-window systems. By targeting green trade corridor development, supporting women and small businesses in cross-border trade, and mobilizing private capital through its commercial arm, Trade Catalyst Africa, TMA directly facilitates trade flow alignment with the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) frameworks.

receiver-org.narrative: TradeMark Africa (TMA) is a leading Aid-for-Trade organisation founded in 2010 to grow intra-African trade, increase Africa’s share in global trade, and make trade more pro-poor and sustainable. We operate on a not-for-profit basis, funded by a strong coalition of development partners including Canada, Denmark, the European Union, Finland, France, the Gates Foundation, Ireland, the Mastercard Foundation, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom. TMA works closely with regional and continental institutions, national governments, the private sector, and civil society to unlock trade and investment opportunities across the continent.
